heroHeadline: New Zealand Frigate Te Mana and Oiler Aotearoa Transit Taiwan Strait (Sep 18) as SCMP Reports US Weighing Delay of $14B Arms Package Until After November APEC, December G20 Summits Ahead of Sept 24 Trump-Xi Meeting
heroSubtitle: New Zealand's Defence Force disclosed Sep 21 that frigate HMNZS Te Mana and oiler HMNZS Aotearoa transited the Taiwan Strait on Sep 18 as part of a three-month Indo-Pacific deployment; PM Christopher Luxon called it 'a routine activity' under international law, and Beijing's defence ministry did not immediately respond — a markedly more restrained reaction than to Aotearoa's November 2025 transit, when PLA forces tracked the vessel and simulated attack runs. Separately, the South China Morning Post reported Sep 19, citing unnamed sources, that the Trump administration is weighing postponing the pending $14 billion Taiwan arms package until after the November APEC summit in Shenzhen and a possible Trump-Xi meeting at the December G20 in Florida, timed around Xi Jinping's Sep 23-25 Washington state visit; one source said Trump had at one point floated delaying the decision to late 2028 or January 2029 before pushback from China hawks. That follows a Sep 17 dispute over a separate report that Beijing had threatened to cancel the summit outright over the same arms package. No new PLA daily sortie/vessel tally was available for Sep 21 at publication time; the most recent confirmed window remains Sep 20's 5 sorties (all crossing the median line) and a 17-ship naval/coast-guard presence, the highest since the Sep 7 surge.
